1	---
2	name: plar
3	description: Map a project's code, UI states and references to pixel-art asset requirements; create or update plar.txt and hand a selected asset to PIXL for production.
4	---
5	
6	PLAR (Pixel Lab Asset Requirements) turns project context into a usable asset work list. Work in the **consumer project's root**, not this skill's installation. The result is `plar.txt`: ordinary JSON with stable asset IDs, source bindings, consumer locations, requirements, destinations and next actions. It describes what is needed; PIXL's PX2 store retains production jobs, candidates and acceptance evidence.
7	
8	## Understand and allocate
9	
10	Read the project's instructions and available source overview/index/MOC, then verify its pointers against the relevant entry points. If no useful overview exists, retain a focused map of the consumers and backend transitions you actually inspect. If it already has `plar.txt`, read the queue and refresh affected rows. Use CodeGraph first when the project has a `.codegraph/` index; otherwise use the host's code tools. Follow actual UI/renderer consumers through imports, manifests, loaders and backend state transitions. Group shared visual roles into one asset with multiple consumers. Attach a newly discovered consumer to the existing asset ID when it uses the same visual role; a new call site alone does not require duplicate art. A function without an image does not automatically need one.
11	
12	Inspect existing art and the visible UI when available. Distinguish missing files, placeholders, reusable assets, visual mismatches and intentionally procedural/text-only elements. Note dynamic paths or unavailable modules in coverage.unresolved. Distinguish a present file deliberately left uninspected from a missing or inaccessible source, and name the inspection boundary. Coverage is authored scope; retain separate evidence for source reads, visual inspection and runtime execution. Scope claims to the code and runtime actually inspected; a filename search is not exhaustive coverage.
13	
14	For each visual role, connect:
15	- Purpose and visible states to file/symbol/usage locations.
16	- Applicable canvas/frame geometry, projection, reference style, edge/alpha policy, timing, pivots, tile rules and import behavior to their sources.
17	- The output destination, checks at the actual display size, dependencies, unresolved choices and one concrete next action.
18	
19	Preserve explicit requirements, observations, proposals and unknowns separately. Use only relevant properties; do not invent a palette, alpha ban or resolution to fill a template. Record user instructions in a small project brief file when they are not already addressable. References convey style; measurements of them do not automatically become rejection rules. When visual input is required, add source-bound references with an explicit role (style, identity, pose, layout, palette, mask or motion) and instructions stating what to preserve.
20	
21	## Save and use
22	
23	Read [the format and operations](references/format.md) when creating or editing the work list. `pixl_plar_save` validates the supplied document, binds new local sources and retains previous versions using an expected hash. `pixl_plar_read` returns queue summaries; pass `asset_id` for the complete selected row and its source/dependency context. Focused reads also return transitive dependency requirements/issues, actual source hashes, absolute project paths, visual references and a derived production view with pending jobs and acceptance state. Use that view to choose resumption versus new preparation; an editable status label is not production evidence. Pass the requirements_hash to a delegate; it changes with relevant requirements or source bytes, not unrelated queue progress. The portable CLI provides the same operations. Ordinary file editing is also supported; re-read and validate afterward.
24	
25	For refresh, read the queue before editing. Its changes report identifies drift and transitive dependents; after a save, or with `plar read --since PRIOR_HASH`, it compares authored requirements against retained history. Treat file-level impact as a prompt to inspect affected consumers, not proof every asset needs regeneration. Check the source overview and changed entry points for newly introduced consumers that no prior row could mention. Preserve unchanged requirements and existing IDs; distinguish a moved destination from a new visual role. Refresh only the source bindings whose dependent claims were reconciled; retain and report pre-existing drift outside that reviewed change instead of globally restamping hashes.
26	
27	A useful row can remain actionable with open questions. Resolve consequential unknowns for the selected action from the project, references or user; continue independent assets. 28	  "reviewer": "EXISTING_ACTOR_ID",
29	  "observed_at": "2026-11-09T16:00:00+00:00",

32	    {"path":"work/render.json","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"live","note":"What the actual destination execution established."}
33	  ],
34	  "verdicts": [
35	    {"criterion":"CURRENT_Q_ID","status":"pass","reason":"Judgment against the literal check.","supersedes":null,"observations":[0]}

44	recording; it is not generated viewing history. Each performed verdict references

46	or `live`). Unavailable verdicts have no observation indices and create no E.
47	Each supplied criterion must belong to this output. `supersedes` names its exact
48	current V or is null when none exists. Omitted criteria retain their current state.

50	An evidence file or schema alone cannot establish that the observation occurred.

52	`action` is explicit: `record` retains judgments; `nominate` also selects this
53	candidate for its output, preserving other output selections; `complete` also

56	activation prerequisites and resolved pending jobs. A failed/unavailable review

60	The current canonical state hash protects publication. The semantic binding hash

66	## Retention, retries and limits
67	
68	Files are captured and copied under `STORE/reviews/<report-sha256>/`; the canonical
69	report contains the request, original paths, retained identities and source state.
70	Auxiliary X records bind retained files, and E binds the report plus candidate/Q
71	semantic scope. Report/file IDs are derived from REVIEW_ID. No supplied source
72	or previous evidence is overwritten. Maximum 64 observations, 64 MiB per file,
73	256 MiB aggregate and 1,024 declared verdicts; reports retain the codec size limit.
74	
75	The operation holds the store lock, checks the complete review/nomination/completion
76	sequence before publishing, then saves ordinary revisions. An interruption may
77	leave immutable unreferenced files or a retained review before completion. Reload
78	the current state hash and repeat the **same REVIEW_ID and observation** to finish;
79	existing review/verdict IDs are reused. Changed payloads, stale bindings or
80	superseded reviews cannot be replayed as new acceptance. A retry never submits a
81	provider job. Changing the review requires a new ID and explicit supersession.
82	
83	Results expose `state_hash` (canonical state), `review_sha256` (report file), current
84	criteria/nomination/task status and publication steps. Immutable snapshot creation
85	status stays separate from current acceptance. The report does not attest reviewer
86	identity, actual viewing or renderer honesty; retained host/runner evidence supplies
87	those observations. Generic source amendment and historical supersession retain
88	their existing PX2 semantics.
89	
90	## Save results directly
91	
92	Use CLI `--result-path work/review-result.json` or MCP `result_path` to save the
93	complete result without transcribing JSON, Windows paths or hashes. The option is
94	available for context, request-review, review-context, candidate-review, family,
95	family-snapshot and PLAR handoff. The path is relative to the explicit consumer
96	root and must be fresh; an existing destination is rejected before the operation.
97	The response contains `result_saved`, the path, file SHA-256, byte count and key
98	status fields. Read the saved file for complete criteria and publication details.
99	CLI full wire context remains PX text; other listed exports contain JSON.
100	
101	If writing fails after an operation publishes, the response has
102	`result_saved:false` and includes the actual `operation_result` (and `wire_result`
103	for wire context). CLI returns a nonzero exit code. Reconcile that result with
104	current state before retrying; a failed file export does not undo publication.
105	Use a fresh path and the operation's existing retry rules. Default output without
106	this option is unchanged; exports do not alter the saved-state format.
107

1	# Compact caller result
2	
3	`plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --view caller` / `pixl_plar_handoff` with
4	`view: "caller"` saves the existing immutable version-1 handoff, then returns a
5	bounded presentation of that same captured selection. The default `view: "receipt"`
6	and saved bytes for identical inputs are unchanged. There is no new ledger, UDL
7	record, provider action or acceptance event.
8	
9	## Agent-authored compact fields
10	
11	`details.status` retains its existing assignment meaning: `delivered`, `partial`,
12	`needs_input` or `blocked`. It does not follow automatically from production state.
13	An optional `details.caller` object supplies the following closed fields:
14	
15	| Field | Content |
16	| --- | --- |
17	| `summary` | Nonempty text, at most 600 characters |
18	| `artifacts` | At most 12 actual project file references |
19	| `reports` | At most 12 references to separately retained detailed reports |
20	| `issues` | At most 12 objects with `category`, `summary` and optional `recovery` |
21	| `integration` | An agent observation with `status`, `summary` and optional `evidence` file references |
22	
23	All fields are optional. Omission means not reported, not a pass or an unavailable
24	check. An absent caller block is returned as `caller.present: false`; arbitrary
25	legacy details are never heuristically summarized. Existing receipt mode does not
26	reinterpret a legacy field called `caller`.
27	
28	File references contain exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`. Paths are nonempty
29	forward-slash project-relative paths, at most 512 characters. SHA-256 is 64 lowercase
30	hexadecimal digits; role is nonempty text of at most 96 characters. The operation
31	confines and hashes every declared artifact, report and integration-evidence file
32	before publishing. It does not copy those files or guarantee that they remain
33	unchanged after that observation. Roles and judgments are supplied by the agent.
34	
35	Issue categories are `invalid_authoring`, `stale_local_state`, `missing_capability`,
36	`uncertain_remote_result`, `unavailable_observation` and `unfinished_work`.
37	Summary and recovery text each have the same 600-character bound. The category is
38	an agent's classification, not an automatic diagnosis or authorization to retry.
39	
40	Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
41	`not_in_scope`. Its summary is required and bounded to 600 characters; evidence
42	uses the same file-reference array. The report labels this block `agent_authored`.
43	A claimed integration pass does not establish a stored verdict or artistic acceptance.
44	
45	The complete caller block must encode to at most 8192 bytes as finite UTF-8 JSON
46	with compact separators. Oversized or malformed blocks, unreadable files and
47	hash mismatches fail before a new handoff is published. Detailed observations
48	belong in linked files or the existing unrestricted expert details, not truncated
49	inside the compact block. `pixl.caller_result.CALLER_SCHEMA` describes the shape.
50	
51	## Returned facts and exact retrieval
52	
53	Caller view retains every default receipt field (`path`, `sha256`, `asset_id`,
54	`requirements_hash`, `state_hash`, `next`, `scope`) and adds:
55	
56	- `assignment`: the supplied status and its `agent_authored` basis.
57	- `caller`: presence, authored fields and the file-verification observation.
58	- `production`: captured task ID/state, selection currency, criterion counts for
59	  current nominees, job counts and delivery facts. Unperformed/unavailable checks
60	  remain unresolved. Counts never imply every operation or visual check succeeded.
61	- `store`: the exact continuation's project-relative production store.
62	- `details_ref` and `resume_ref`: immutable file path/hash, physical line range,
63	  UTF-8 byte count and JSON pointer for the saved section.
64	- `resume_inline`, `resume_bytes`, and the unchanged `resume` when it occupies at
65	  most 4096 compact UTF-8 JSON bytes. Larger continuations are omitted as a whole
66	  and remain retrievable through `resume_ref`; there is no partial rewritten resume.
67	- `refresh`: the exact focused `pixl_plar_read` operation and arguments. Reread
68	  after state or source changes and compare requirements/state identities before
69	  acting. This operation is a read instruction, not automatic execution.
70	
71	Delivery remains exactly the existing handoff's derived delivery value. If larger
72	than 2048 compact JSON bytes, `production.delivery_inline` is false and
73	`delivery_ref` identifies `/resume/delivery`; the containing resume line range is
74	returned intact. `delivery_complete` and `delivery_observed` remain visible.
75	Destination bytes and declared family criteria do not establish undeclared engine
76	or artistic checks. Assignment status remains independent even when delivery is
77	complete or an external destination subsequently changes without a state revision.
78	
79	Use existing `source` / `pixl_source` with the locator's path, SHA-256, line bounds
80	and an adequate byte budget. The field slice is exact JSON source text and can
81	include its trailing object-member comma. The JSON pointer identifies its meaning;
82	no new reader tool is required. A larger section may be read in smaller physical
83	line ranges under the same file hash. When parsing as an object, open the complete
84	immutable file or wrap the returned member after removing its trailing comma.
85	
86	Caller-view errors use `caller_result_input`, `caller_result_size`,
87	`caller_artifact_unavailable` and `caller_artifact_stale`; existing `path_escape`,
88	`handoff_stale`, `handoff_state` and `handoff_corrupt` retain their meaning. A file
89	failure identifies the declared file's `path` and `expected_file_sha256`; a hash
90	mismatch also returns `observed_file_sha256`. Its allocation `plar_path` stays
91	separate from that artifact path in structured diagnostics. A file
92	export failure does not undo an already saved handoff. Reconcile its returned
93	operation result before repeating the save; never treat it as a reason to repeat
94	remote generation.
95

content.text:
# MCP Tool: create_character

Queue a character with 4 or 8 directions. Returns its id at once; poll
get_character (~2-5 min).

Modes (default v3):
- v3: the most detailed sprites, 8 directions, up to 256px, drawn from the
  description as written. Humanoid only without a reference.
- v3 + reference image is the default way to turn a sprite you have into a
  character (not create_8_direction_object): kept as drawn as the south view,
  so it must face the viewer straight on. Humanoids and quadrupeds;
  direction_images adds directions you drew.
- pro: 8 directions, max 128px. To match an existing character
  (style_character_id) or a style picture, design from concept art, or rotate a
  sprite facing any way or a body v3 gets wrong (Pro rotate). The only mode
  taking palette and max_colors.
- standard: the cheapest, 4 or 8 directions, max 128px.

A quadruped from text: create_character_pro_flash(template_id=...) at 64px, or
mode="pro" or "standard" here with body_type="quadruped". No seed; for one look
across characters use style_character_id or a reference image.

Cost: standard 1 generation at ANY size. v3 from text by size: 2 for 16-90, 3
for 91-128, 4 for 129-156, 5 for 157-181, 6 for 182-202, 7 for 203-221, 8 for
222-239, 9 for 240-256; with a reference, ceil(w*h*8/65536) of its own
size, minimum 1 (64x64 = 1, 128x128 = 2); every direction yours is an import,
0.25. pro 10 up to 85px, 15 for 86-113, 25 for 114-128, which is also its size
cap.

Full reference (all rules, sizes and prices): search_help(tool="create_character").

## Parameters
- `description` (str, required) — Character appearance, e.g. 'cute wizard with blue robes'. v3 without a reference draws a two-armed, two-legged figure whatever this says; for an animal see body_type.
- `name` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Character name, e.g. 'Blue Wizard'.
- `body_type` (Literal["humanoid", "quadruped"], optional) [default: humanoid] — "quadruped" (4-legged animals) needs template. Quadrupeds work in mode="standard", mode="pro", and mode="v3" WITH a reference image; v3 without a reference image is humanoid only.
- `template` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Required with body_type='quadruped': `bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`. Ignored for humanoids.
- `mode` (Literal["standard", "pro", "v3"], optional) [default: v3] — Default "v3". See the tool description for when to pick each.
- `n_directions` (Literal[4, 8], optional) [default: 8] — Ignored in pro and in v3 without a reference (always 8). With a v3 reference, 4 keeps south/east/north/west.
- `reference_image_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — reference_image_url as PNG base64 (max 256x256): for v3 it must face straight-on, toward the viewer. Prefer the URL above ~32x32: clients truncate long base64.
- `style_character_id` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — pro only: id of your completed 8-direction character whose style the new one copies; its drawn part (not its canvas) must fit size, and an unset size follows it. Not with a reference image.
- `style_image_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — pro only: a pixel-art picture whose style the new character copies (https, upload:<id> or data: URL); its visible part must fit size, max 128. Not with a reference image.
- `style_image_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — style_image_url as PNG base64.
- `reference_image_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — https, data: or `upload:<id>` URL of the sprite to rotate (v3 or pro, max 256x256). v3 takes it as south: it must face STRAIGHT-ON, toward the viewer, or a 3/4 view offsets every direction; there is no way to declare a different facing. pro: any facing.
- `concept_image_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — pro only: concept art, a painting or a photo the character is designed from (look kept, not pose); https, data: or `upload:<id>` URL. A finished sprite to rotate goes in reference_image_url.
- `concept_image_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — concept_image_url as PNG/JPEG base64.
- `direction_images` (Optional[dict[str, str]], optional) [default: None] — v3 with a reference only: sprites you drew for other directions (URL, upload:<id>, data URL or PNG base64), same canvas as the reference, used as drawn; v3 draws the rest.
- `proportions` (Optional[str], optional) [default: {"type": "preset", "name": "default"}] — Standard, humanoids: {"type": "preset", "name": "chibi"}, presets default, chibi, cartoon, stylized, realistic_male, realistic_female, heroic; or "custom" bone sizes (format in the full reference).
- `size` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — Pixels, default 48 (with a reference: its own size). Max 128 in standard and pro; v3 from text takes multiples of 4. Standard stores it on a ~40% larger canvas (64 -> 92x92).
- `outline` (Optional[Literal["single color black outline", "single color outline", "selective outline", "lineless"]], optional) [default: single color black outline] — Soft hint. Ignored in pro.
- `shading` (Optional[Literal["flat shading", "basic shading", "medium shading", "detailed shading"]], optional) [default: basic shading] — Soft hint. Ignored in pro and v3.
- `detail` (Optional[Literal["low detail", "medium detail", "high detail"]], optional) [default: medium detail] — Soft hint. Ignored in pro.
- `text_guidance_scale` (float, optional) [default: 8.0] — How closely to follow the description. Ignored in pro and v3.
- `view` (Literal["low top-down", "high top-down", "side", "oblique"], optional) [default: low top-down] — Camera: "low top-down" (~20°, classic 3/4 RPG), "high top-down" (~35°), "side" (eye level), "oblique" (beta: standard, n_directions=4, max 128px).
- `palette` (Optional[list[str]], optional) [default: None] — Target palette, 2 to 256 hex colours as a JSON array, e.g. ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"] for Game Boy or ["#000000", "#ffffff"] for 1-bit. Every pixel the tool draws is one of them; pixels you supplied (a direction you drew) stay as they are.
- `palette_name` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Optional name of the palette (e.g. 'Game Boy', 'PICO-8'); naming it helps the look. It only LABELS the colours you pass in palette rather than looking any up, so it cannot be sent on its own.
- `max_colors` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — At most this many colours (2-64). With a palette, they are picked from it. On the three tools that have a standard mode — create_character, create_topdown_tileset, animate_object — ANY palette setting needs mode='pro': standard refuses palette and max_colors, alone or together. Every other tool taking them has no standard mode and accepts them always.

# create_character: full reference

Queue character creation. Returns immediately with character ID. Use get_character to
check status. It takes NO seed and cannot be made reproducible — unusually for the
family, since create_character_pro_flash and create_character_state both do; to keep a
look across characters pass style_character_id or a reference image instead.

## Which mode
v3 (default) for heroes, enemies and NPCs: clearly more detailed sprites than standard,
2 generations up to 88 px. For a quadruped from text, create_character_pro_flash(
template_id=...) at 64 px (6 generations), or mode="pro" or mode="standard" here; v3
draws one only from a reference sprite. Pro when a new character must match an existing
one (style_character_id) or an uploaded style picture (style_image_url), or to follow
concept art. Standard for the lowest cost.

To turn a sprite you already have into a character, v3 + reference image is the default
way: cheapest, and the sprite stays exactly as drawn as the south view. Pro + reference
image (Pro rotate) when the sprite does not face the viewer straight on (3/4, side or
back view) or the body is one v3 gets wrong (a creature that is not a standing humanoid
or four-legged animal: v3 assumes one and tends to add limbs).

## Modes
- standard: template-based skeleton generation (cheaper, 1 generation), 4 or 8
  directions, ~2-5 min. Style params are soft guidance (the model tries to follow them
  but results may vary). Max 128px.
- pro: AI reference-based generation for higher quality, 10-25 generations depending on
  size, always 8 directions, max 128px. Ignores all style/proportions params: pro mode
  ignores n_directions, outline, shading, detail, text_guidance_scale, and proportions.
  Accepts style_character_id to match an existing 8-direction character's style,
  style_image_url to copy an uploaded picture's pixel style, concept_image_url to design
  the character from concept art, a painting or a photo, and reference_image_url to
  rotate a sprite that faces any way (Pro rotate).
  Pro mode only: pass `palette` (hex colours, plus `palette_name`) for a console or
  palette look (1-bit, Game Boy, PICO-8, any Lospec palette): all 8 directions are drawn
  for it and every pixel is one of its colours. `max_colors` is Pro-only too.
- v3: the highest quality output, 2-9 generations depending on size, 8 directions, up
  to 256px. Outline and detail are soft guidance; v3 mode ignores shading, proportions,
  and text_guidance_scale. The sprite is drawn from description as written: describe
  pose, outfit, materials and colours yourself. v3 honours n_directions only with a
  reference image (without one it is always 8).
- v3 + reference_image_base64 / reference_image_url: rotates YOUR south-facing sprite
  into 8 (or 4) directions — use this (not create_8_direction_object) to turn an
  existing character sprite into a full character. Works for humanoids and quadrupeds
  (pass body_type="quadruped" + template). Add direction_images for directions you
  already drew; v3 fills only the rest. direction_images is v3 only.
- v3 without a reference image draws the sprite itself and is humanoid only (its sprite
  generator only draws humanoids): a slime or a bird comes out as a two-armed,
  two-legged figure whatever the description says.

Body types:
- Humanoid: bipedal characters (people, robots) with proportion customization.
- Quadruped: 4-legged animals — requires the template param (`bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`).
  Quadrupeds work in mode="standard", mode="pro", and mode="v3" WITH a reference image
  (south-facing sprite + template); v3 without a reference image is humanoid only.

## Cost
The mode decides it, and standard is the cheap one — 1 generation at ANY size, 4 or 8
directions. mode='v3' from scratch draws the sprite AND its 8 rotations, by longest
side: 2 for 16-90; 3 for 91-128; 4 for 129-156; 5 for 157-181; 6 for 182-202; 7 for
203-221; 8 for 222-239; 9 for 240-256. Passing a reference sprite drops the drawing
step and prices the reference's OWN width times height — ceil(w*h*8/65536), minimum 1 —
NOT the square ladder above, so a tall sprite is cheap: 64x64, 48x80 and 64x96 are all
1, 128x128 is 2, and 32x256 is 1 where drawing it from text would be 9. Setting size
makes the output square, and then the square rule applies. Supplying every direction
yourself is an import, 0.25 generations. mode='pro' prices a 3x3
grid and is the dear one, with or without a reference: 10 up to 85px, 15 for 86-113, 25
for 114-128, which is also its size cap (v3 is the only mode that reaches 256px).

## Parameters
- description: character appearance (e.g. 'cute wizard with blue robes'). v3 without a
  reference draws a two-armed, two-legged figure whatever this says (a slime or a bird
  comes out humanoid); for an animal see body_type.
- name: character name for reference (e.g. 'Blue Wizard', 'Tabby Cat').
- body_type: "humanoid" for bipedal characters (people, robots). "quadruped" for
  4-legged animals - requires the `template` parameter. Available quadruped templates:
  `bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`.
- template: quadruped template to use (required when body_type='quadruped'). Available:
  `bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`. Ignored for humanoid body type.
- n_directions: number of directional views (4 or 8). Ignored in pro mode and in v3
  without a reference image (always 8). With a v3 reference, 4 keeps
  south/east/north/west.
- reference_image_base64 / reference_image_url: the character sprite to rotate (PNG
  base64, or an https URL to the sprite PNG; max 256x256), facing south for v3. Give a
  url OR a base64, not both. With mode="v3" (the default way) it rotates this exact
  sprite into 8 directions — the right tool for turning an existing character sprite
  into a full rotating character (do NOT use create_8_direction_object for characters).
  The image defines identity and style; description guides the rotation; outline/detail
  hints are ignored. SOUTH MEANS STRAIGHT-ON, FACING THE VIEWER: whatever this sprite
  faces is taken as south and every other direction is rotated from it, so a 3/4 turn
  here silently offsets the WHOLE set by 45 degrees and every direction label is wrong.
  There is no way to declare a different facing in v3 — re-pose or pick a front-on
  reference first, or you pay for eight unusable sprites. Output size defaults to the
  reference's own dimensions unless size is set. With mode="pro" (Pro rotate, 10-25
  generations) the sprite may face any way, and Pro draws all 8 directions from it: pick
  it for a 3/4, side or back view, or a body v3 gets wrong (a creature that is not a
  standing humanoid or four-legged animal: v3 assumes one and tends to add limbs). Pro
  trims the transparent border and needs the visible sprite to fit 128x128; size
  defaults to its visible size (at least 32). PREFER reference_image_url for anything
  above ~32x32 — MCP clients routinely truncate large inline base64 (cut off
  mid-string), which corrupts the image.
- style_character_id (mode="pro" only): ID of one of your existing 8-direction
  characters to use as the style reference. Its 8 directional sprites guide the new
  character's style in every direction. The style character must be completed with 8
  directions, and size must be at least its sprite content size — the job fails fast
  with the required size otherwise. Not with a reference image (Pro rotate keeps the
  sprite's own look).
- style_image_url / style_image_base64 (mode="pro" only): a pixel-art picture whose
  pixel scale, proportions and rendering the new character copies (the creator's style
  reference; without one Pro uses a default style for the view). An https, upload:<id>
  or data: URL, or the picture as PNG base64; give a url OR a base64, not both. Its
  transparent border is trimmed and the rest goes whole into the middle of Pro's grid,
  so it must fit size: size defaults to its visible size (at least 32, at most 128).
  Combines with concept_image_url and style_character_id. Not with a reference image:
  to rotate a sprite as drawn, pass it as reference_image_url instead.
- concept_image_url / concept_image_base64 (mode="pro" only): concept art, a painting,
  sketch or photo of the character (any pose or angle; larger than 1024 px is scaled
  down to fit) that the 8 directions are designed from. The result keeps its look, not
  its pose or canvas. An https or data: URL, or the concept as PNG/JPEG base64; give a
  url OR a base64, not both. For a finished sprite you want rotated as drawn, use
  mode="v3" with reference_image_url instead.
- direction_images: requires mode="v3" and a reference image: sprites you already drew
  for OTHER directions, as {direction: image}. Directions: south-east, east,
  north-east, north, north-west, west, south-west (with n_directions=4 only east, north,
  west). Each image is an https URL, upload:<id>, data URL, or PNG base64, like the
  reference. They are used exactly as drawn and v3 generates only the directions you
  leave out; cover every one and nothing is generated (import, 0.25
  generations). Every image must have the same canvas size as the reference and face
  the direction it is keyed under. If your client cannot send an object here, send the
  same object JSON-encoded as a string.
- proportions: character body proportions as a JSON string (humanoid only, ignored for
  quadrupeds; standard mode only). PRESET: built-in proportions like
  '{"type": "preset", "name": "chibi"}' (options: default, chibi, cartoon, stylized,
  realistic_male, realistic_female, heroic). CUSTOM: exact values like
  '{"type": "custom", "head_size": 1.5, "arms_length": 0.8, "legs_length": 0.9,
  "shoulder_width": 0.7, "hip_width": 0.8}' (all values 0.5-2.0).
- size: character size in pixels (default 48). Max 128 for standard/pro mode; up to 256
  for mode="v3". Standard mode treats this as the size of the character and stores it
  on a canvas ~40% larger (64 -> 92x92, 128 -> 180x180) so animations fit. Pro mode
  stores rotations on a shared square canvas at least this large. V3 from scratch sends
  this as the requested square generation size (a multiple of 4); with a v3 reference
  image, omitted size uses the reference dimensions and a supplied size is advisory.
- outline: outline style hint (soft guidance — the model may not follow exactly).
  Ignored in pro mode.
- shading: shading hint (soft guidance — the model may not follow exactly). Ignored in
  pro and v3 modes.
- detail: detail level hint (soft guidance — the model may not follow exactly). Ignored
  in pro mode.
- text_guidance_scale: how closely to follow the text description (higher=more
  faithful). Default 8.0. Ignored in pro and v3 modes.
- view: camera angle. "low top-down" (~20° from above, classic 3/4 RPG), "high
  top-down" (~35° steeper angle), "side" (eye-level), "oblique" (BETA: 3/4 oblique
  projection, max 128px, 4-dir only, standard mode only).


## Usage
```python
create_character(
    description=...,
)
```

# MCP Tool: create_object_pro_flash

Create a Pro Flash object from text, with one direction or eight V3 views.

Supply description, optional width/height (default 64x64), and style_image.
For props that match a game's characters, pass the same anchor sprite as
style_image on every call (e.g. the hero's south rotation URL from
get_character); without it each call picks its own look.
Custom sizes (Beta) accept width and height from 16 to 256 in multiples of 4 pixels.
First-direction generation is built into this call. n_directions=1 charges
for one new image; n_directions=8 also charges for rotations. Alternatively
reuse source_image_id or first_frame_url/base64 and omit size/style settings:
saving one direction is then free, and eight views charge only rotations.
A generated first frame always faces the viewer (south), whatever the
description says. For a profile or other facing with n_directions=1, make
it with create_image_pro_flash and pass its id as source_image_id.
Objects remain objects without skeletons. Poll get_object(object_id), then
download its PNG (one direction) or ZIP (eight). No preview is regenerated.

Cost: n_directions=1 is the image alone, by longest side — 5 generations up
to 96px, 6 from 100 to 208, 9 from 212 to 256 — so 32x96 and 64x48 are both
5. n_directions=8 adds a rotation charge, billed separately, and the
TOTAL by longest side is the same ladder the character tool uses:
6 for 16-88; 7 for 92-96; 8 for 100-128; 9 for 132-156; 10 for 160-180; 11 for 184-200; 12 for 204-208; 15 for 212-220; 16 for 224-236; 17 for 240-256. The steps are uneven, so read the band rather than interpolating;
get_pro_flash_capabilities(operation="object", width=, height=,
n_directions=) quotes the split for free. Reusing a first frame bills only the rotation
part, and nothing at all for one direction.

## Parameters
- `description` (str, required)
- `source_image_id` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None]
- `first_frame_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None]
- `first_frame_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None]
- `name` (str, optional) [default: ]
- `view` (Literal["low top-down", "high top-down", "side"], optional) [default: low top-down]
- `first_frame_direction` (Literal["south"], optional) [default: south]
- `n_directions` (Literal[1, 8], optional) [default: 8]
- `seed` (int, optional) [default: 0]
- `width` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — Defaults to 64 for text creation. Native sizes: 16x16 (experimental), 24x24, 32x32, 32x48, 48x48, 64x64, 96x64, 96x96, 128x128. Custom size (Beta): integer width 16–256 and height 16–256. Both dimensions must be multiples of 4 pixels. Pixel-grid recovery uses image-to-pixel-art with fixer when needed. No native image resizing.
- `height` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None]
- `style_image` (Optional[ProFlashReferenceInput], optional) [default: None] — Style anchor. Exactly ONE of its three sources: `url` also accepts an `upload:<id>` from get_upload_url or a data: URL, and `source_image_id` is an image you own (what a Pro Flash job returns). It must fit INSIDE the output canvas both ways — a larger one is refused, so crop it; resizing pixel art is never the answer. Reuse one anchor across calls to keep a set consistent.
- `style_options` (Optional[ProFlashStyleOptions], optional) [default: None]
- `palette` (Optional[list[str]], optional) [default: None] — Target palette, 2 to 256 hex colours as a JSON array, e.g. ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"] for Game Boy or ["#000000", "#ffffff"] for 1-bit. Every pixel the tool draws is one of them; pixels you supplied (a direction you drew) stay as they are.
- `palette_name` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Optional name of the palette (e.g. 'Game Boy', 'PICO-8'); naming it helps the look. It only LABELS the colours you pass in palette rather than looking any up, so it cannot be sent on its own.
- `max_colors` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — At most this many colours (2-64). With a palette, they are picked from it. On the three tools that have a standard mode — create_character, create_topdown_tileset, animate_object — ANY palette setting needs mode='pro': standard refuses palette and max_colors, alone or together. Every other tool taking them has no standard mode and accepts them always.

## Usage
```python
create_object_pro_flash(
    description=...,
)
```

# MCP Tool: create_character

Queue a character with 4 or 8 directions. Returns its id at once; poll
get_character (~2-5 min).

Modes (default v3):
- v3: the most detailed sprites, 8 directions, up to 256px, drawn from the
  description as written. Humanoid only without a reference.
- v3 + reference image is the default way to turn a sprite you have into a
  character (not create_8_direction_object): kept as drawn as the south view,
  so it must face the viewer straight on. Humanoids and quadrupeds;
  direction_images adds directions you drew.
- pro: 8 directions, max 128px. To match an existing character
  (style_character_id) or a style picture, design from concept art, or rotate a
  sprite facing any way or a body v3 gets wrong (Pro rotate). The only mode
  taking palette and max_colors.
- standard: the cheapest, 4 or 8 directions, max 128px.

A quadruped from text: create_character_pro_flash(template_id=...) at 64px, or
mode="pro" or "standard" here with body_type="quadruped". No seed; for one look
across characters use style_character_id or a reference image.

Cost: standard 1 generation at ANY size. v3 from text by size: 2 for 16-90, 3
for 91-128, 4 for 129-156, 5 for 157-181, 6 for 182-202, 7 for 203-221, 8 for
222-239, 9 for 240-256; with a reference, ceil(w*h*8/65536) of its own
size, minimum 1 (64x64 = 1, 128x128 = 2); every direction yours is an import,
0.25. pro 10 up to 85px, 15 for 86-113, 25 for 114-128, which is also its size
cap.

Full reference (all rules, sizes and prices): search_help(tool="create_character").

## Parameters
- `description` (str, required) — Character appearance, e.g. 'cute wizard with blue robes'. v3 without a reference draws a two-armed, two-legged figure whatever this says; for an animal see body_type.
- `name` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Character name, e.g. 'Blue Wizard'.
- `body_type` (Literal["humanoid", "quadruped"], optional) [default: humanoid] — "quadruped" (4-legged animals) needs template. Quadrupeds work in mode="standard", mode="pro", and mode="v3" WITH a reference image; v3 without a reference image is humanoid only.
- `template` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Required with body_type='quadruped': `bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`. Ignored for humanoids.
- `mode` (Literal["standard", "pro", "v3"], optional) [default: v3] — Default "v3". See the tool description for when to pick each.
- `n_directions` (Literal[4, 8], optional) [default: 8] — Ignored in pro and in v3 without a reference (always 8). With a v3 reference, 4 keeps south/east/north/west.
- `reference_image_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — reference_image_url as PNG base64 (max 256x256): for v3 it must face straight-on, toward the viewer. Prefer the URL above ~32x32: clients truncate long base64.
- `style_character_id` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — pro only: id of your completed 8-direction character whose style the new one copies; its drawn part (not its canvas) must fit size, and an unset size follows it. Not with a reference image.
- `style_image_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — pro only: a pixel-art picture whose style the new character copies (https, upload:<id> or data: URL); its visible part must fit size, max 128. Not with a reference image.
- `style_image_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — style_image_url as PNG base64.
- `reference_image_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — https, data: or `upload:<id>` URL of the sprite to rotate (v3 or pro, max 256x256). v3 takes it as south: it must face STRAIGHT-ON, toward the viewer, or a 3/4 view offsets every direction; there is no way to declare a different facing. pro: any facing.
- `concept_image_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — pro only: concept art, a painting or a photo the character is designed from (look kept, not pose); https, data: or `upload:<id>` URL. A finished sprite to rotate goes in reference_image_url.
- `concept_image_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — concept_image_url as PNG/JPEG base64.
- `direction_images` (Optional[dict[str, str]], optional) [default: None] — v3 with a reference only: sprites you drew for other directions (URL, upload:<id>, data URL or PNG base64), same canvas as the reference, used as drawn; v3 draws the rest.
- `proportions` (Optional[str], optional) [default: {"type": "preset", "name": "default"}] — Standard, humanoids: {"type": "preset", "name": "chibi"}, presets default, chibi, cartoon, stylized, realistic_male, realistic_female, heroic; or "custom" bone sizes (format in the full reference).
- `size` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — Pixels, default 48 (with a reference: its own size). Max 128 in standard and pro; v3 from text takes multiples of 4. Standard stores it on a ~40% larger canvas (64 -> 92x92).
- `outline` (Optional[Literal["single color black outline", "single color outline", "selective outline", "lineless"]], optional) [default: single color black outline] — Soft hint. Ignored in pro.
- `shading` (Optional[Literal["flat shading", "basic shading", "medium shading", "detailed shading"]], optional) [default: basic shading] — Soft hint. Ignored in pro and v3.
- `detail` (Optional[Literal["low detail", "medium detail", "high detail"]], optional) [default: medium detail] — Soft hint. Ignored in pro.
- `text_guidance_scale` (float, optional) [default: 8.0] — How closely to follow the description. Ignored in pro and v3.
- `view` (Literal["low top-down", "high top-down", "side", "oblique"], optional) [default: low top-down] — Camera: "low top-down" (~20°, classic 3/4 RPG), "high top-down" (~35°), "side" (eye level), "oblique" (beta: standard, n_directions=4, max 128px).
- `palette` (Optional[list[str]], optional) [default: None] — Target palette, 2 to 256 hex colours as a JSON array, e.g. ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"] for Game Boy or ["#000000", "#ffffff"] for 1-bit. Every pixel the tool draws is one of them; pixels you supplied (a direction you drew) stay as they are.
- `palette_name` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Optional name of the palette (e.g. 'Game Boy', 'PICO-8'); naming it helps the look. It only LABELS the colours you pass in palette rather than looking any up, so it cannot be sent on its own.
- `max_colors` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — At most this many colours (2-64). With a palette, they are picked from it. On the three tools that have a standard mode — create_character, create_topdown_tileset, animate_object — ANY palette setting needs mode='pro': standard refuses palette and max_colors, alone or together. Every other tool taking them has no standard mode and accepts them always.

# create_character: full reference

Queue character creation. Returns immediately with character ID. Use get_character to
check status. It takes NO seed and cannot be made reproducible — unusually for the
family, since create_character_pro_flash and create_character_state both do; to keep a
look across characters pass style_character_id or a reference image instead.

## Which mode
v3 (default) for heroes, enemies and NPCs: clearly more detailed sprites than standard,
2 generations up to 88 px. For a quadruped from text, create_character_pro_flash(
template_id=...) at 64 px (6 generations), or mode="pro" or mode="standard" here; v3
draws one only from a reference sprite. Pro when a new character must match an existing
one (style_character_id) or an uploaded style picture (style_image_url), or to follow
concept art. Standard for the lowest cost.

To turn a sprite you already have into a character, v3 + reference image is the default
way: cheapest, and the sprite stays exactly as drawn as the south view. Pro + reference
image (Pro rotate) when the sprite does not face the viewer straight on (3/4, side or
back view) or the body is one v3 gets wrong (a creature that is not a standing humanoid
or four-legged animal: v3 assumes one and tends to add limbs).

## Modes
- standard: template-based skeleton generation (cheaper, 1 generation), 4 or 8
  directions, ~2-5 min. Style params are soft guidance (the model tries to follow them
  but results may vary). Max 128px.
- pro: AI reference-based generation for higher quality, 10-25 generations depending on
  size, always 8 directions, max 128px. Ignores all style/proportions params: pro mode
  ignores n_directions, outline, shading, detail, text_guidance_scale, and proportions.
  Accepts style_character_id to match an existing 8-direction character's style,
  style_image_url to copy an uploaded picture's pixel style, concept_image_url to design
  the character from concept art, a painting or a photo, and reference_image_url to
  rotate a sprite that faces any way (Pro rotate).
  Pro mode only: pass `palette` (hex colours, plus `palette_name`) for a console or
  palette look (1-bit, Game Boy, PICO-8, any Lospec palette): all 8 directions are drawn
  for it and every pixel is one of its colours. `max_colors` is Pro-only too.
- v3: the highest quality output, 2-9 generations depending on size, 8 directions, up
  to 256px. Outline and detail are soft guidance; v3 mode ignores shading, proportions,
  and text_guidance_scale. The sprite is drawn from description as written: describe
  pose, outfit, materials and colours yourself. v3 honours n_directions only with a
  reference image (without one it is always 8).
- v3 + reference_image_base64 / reference_image_url: rotates YOUR south-facing sprite
  into 8 (or 4) directions — use this (not create_8_direction_object) to turn an
  existing character sprite into a full character. Works for humanoids and quadrupeds
  (pass body_type="quadruped" + template). Add direction_images for directions you
  already drew; v3 fills only the rest. direction_images is v3 only.
- v3 without a reference image draws the sprite itself and is humanoid only (its sprite
  generator only draws humanoids): a slime or a bird comes out as a two-armed,
  two-legged figure whatever the description says.

Body types:
- Humanoid: bipedal characters (people, robots) with proportion customization.
- Quadruped: 4-legged animals — requires the template param (`bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`).
  Quadrupeds work in mode="standard", mode="pro", and mode="v3" WITH a reference image
  (south-facing sprite + template); v3 without a reference image is humanoid only.

## Cost
The mode decides it, and standard is the cheap one — 1 generation at ANY size, 4 or 8
directions. mode='v3' from scratch draws the sprite AND its 8 rotations, by longest
side: 2 for 16-90; 3 for 91-128; 4 for 129-156; 5 for 157-181; 6 for 182-202; 7 for
203-221; 8 for 222-239; 9 for 240-256. Passing a reference sprite drops the drawing
step and prices the reference's OWN width times height — ceil(w*h*8/65536), minimum 1 —
NOT the square ladder above, so a tall sprite is cheap: 64x64, 48x80 and 64x96 are all
1, 128x128 is 2, and 32x256 is 1 where drawing it from text would be 9. Setting size
makes the output square, and then the square rule applies. Supplying every direction
yourself is an import, 0.25 generations. mode='pro' prices a 3x3
grid and is the dear one, with or without a reference: 10 up to 85px, 15 for 86-113, 25
for 114-128, which is also its size cap (v3 is the only mode that reaches 256px).

## Parameters
- description: character appearance (e.g. 'cute wizard with blue robes'). v3 without a
  reference draws a two-armed, two-legged figure whatever this says (a slime or a bird
  comes out humanoid); for an animal see body_type.
- name: character name for reference (e.g. 'Blue Wizard', 'Tabby Cat').
- body_type: "humanoid" for bipedal characters (people, robots). "quadruped" for
  4-legged animals - requires the `template` parameter. Available quadruped templates:
  `bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`.
- template: quadruped template to use (required when body_type='quadruped'). Available:
  `bear`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `lion`. Ignored for humanoid body type.
- n_directions: number of directional views (4 or 8). Ignored in pro mode and in v3
  without a reference image (always 8). With a v3 reference, 4 keeps
  south/east/north/west.
- reference_image_base64 / reference_image_url: the character sprite to rotate (PNG
  base64, or an https URL to the sprite PNG; max 256x256), facing south for v3. Give a
  url OR a base64, not both. With mode="v3" (the default way) it rotates this exact
  sprite into 8 directions — the right tool for turning an existing character sprite
  into a full rotating character (do NOT use create_8_direction_object for characters).
  The image defines identity and style; description guides the rotation; outline/detail
  hints are ignored. SOUTH MEANS STRAIGHT-ON, FACING THE VIEWER: whatever this sprite
  faces is taken as south and every other direction is rotated from it, so a 3/4 turn
  here silently offsets the WHOLE set by 45 degrees and every direction label is wrong.
  There is no way to declare a different facing in v3 — re-pose or pick a front-on
  reference first, or you pay for eight unusable sprites. Output size defaults to the
  reference's own dimensions unless size is set. With mode="pro" (Pro rotate, 10-25
  generations) the sprite may face any way, and Pro draws all 8 directions from it: pick
  it for a 3/4, side or back view, or a body v3 gets wrong (a creature that is not a
  standing humanoid or four-legged animal: v3 assumes one and tends to add limbs). Pro
  trims the transparent border and needs the visible sprite to fit 128x128; size
  defaults to its visible size (at least 32). PREFER reference_image_url for anything
  above ~32x32 — MCP clients routinely truncate large inline base64 (cut off
  mid-string), which corrupts the image.
- style_character_id (mode="pro" only): ID of one of your existing 8-direction
  characters to use as the style reference. Its 8 directional sprites guide the new
  character's style in every direction. The style character must be completed with 8
  directions, and size must be at least its sprite content size — the job fails fast
  with the required size otherwise. Not with a reference image (Pro rotate keeps the
  sprite's own look).
- style_image_url / style_image_base64 (mode="pro" only): a pixel-art picture whose
  pixel scale, proportions and rendering the new character copies (the creator's style
  reference; without one Pro uses a default style for the view). An https, upload:<id>
  or data: URL, or the picture as PNG base64; give a url OR a base64, not both. Its
  transparent border is trimmed and the rest goes whole into the middle of Pro's grid,
  so it must fit size: size defaults to its visible size (at least 32, at most 128).
  Combines with concept_image_url and style_character_id. Not with a reference image:
  to rotate a sprite as drawn, pass it as reference_image_url instead.
- concept_image_url / concept_image_base64 (mode="pro" only): concept art, a painting,
  sketch or photo of the character (any pose or angle; larger than 1024 px is scaled
  down to fit) that the 8 directions are designed from. The result keeps its look, not
  its pose or canvas. An https or data: URL, or the concept as PNG/JPEG base64; give a
  url OR a base64, not both. For a finished sprite you want rotated as drawn, use
  mode="v3" with reference_image_url instead.
- direction_images: requires mode="v3" and a reference image: sprites you already drew
  for OTHER directions, as {direction: image}. Directions: south-east, east,
  north-east, north, north-west, west, south-west (with n_directions=4 only east, north,
  west). Each image is an https URL, upload:<id>, data URL, or PNG base64, like the
  reference. They are used exactly as drawn and v3 generates only the directions you
  leave out; cover every one and nothing is generated (import, 0.25
  generations). Every image must have the same canvas size as the reference and face
  the direction it is keyed under. If your client cannot send an object here, send the
  same object JSON-encoded as a string.
- proportions: character body proportions as a JSON string (humanoid only, ignored for
  quadrupeds; standard mode only). PRESET: built-in proportions like
  '{"type": "preset", "name": "chibi"}' (options: default, chibi, cartoon, stylized,
  realistic_male, realistic_female, heroic). CUSTOM: exact values like
  '{"type": "custom", "head_size": 1.5, "arms_length": 0.8, "legs_length": 0.9,
  "shoulder_width": 0.7, "hip_width": 0.8}' (all values 0.5-2.0).
- size: character size in pixels (default 48). Max 128 for standard/pro mode; up to 256
  for mode="v3". Standard mode treats this as the size of the character and stores it
  on a canvas ~40% larger (64 -> 92x92, 128 -> 180x180) so animations fit. Pro mode
  stores rotations on a shared square canvas at least this large. V3 from scratch sends
  this as the requested square generation size (a multiple of 4); with a v3 reference
  image, omitted size uses the reference dimensions and a supplied size is advisory.
- outline: outline style hint (soft guidance — the model may not follow exactly).
  Ignored in pro mode.
- shading: shading hint (soft guidance — the model may not follow exactly). Ignored in
  pro and v3 modes.
- detail: detail level hint (soft guidance — the model may not follow exactly). Ignored
  in pro mode.
- text_guidance_scale: how closely to follow the text description (higher=more
  faithful). Default 8.0. Ignored in pro and v3 modes.
- view: camera angle. "low top-down" (~20° from above, classic 3/4 RPG), "high
  top-down" (~35° steeper angle), "side" (eye-level), "oblique" (BETA: 3/4 oblique
  projection, max 128px, 4-dir only, standard mode only).


## Usage
```python
create_character(
    description=...,
)
```

# MCP Tool: create_object_pro_flash

Create a Pro Flash object from text, with one direction or eight V3 views.

Supply description, optional width/height (default 64x64), and style_image.
For props that match a game's characters, pass the same anchor sprite as
style_image on every call (e.g. the hero's south rotation URL from
get_character); without it each call picks its own look.
Custom sizes (Beta) accept width and height from 16 to 256 in multiples of 4 pixels.
First-direction generation is built into this call. n_directions=1 charges
for one new image; n_directions=8 also charges for rotations. Alternatively
reuse source_image_id or first_frame_url/base64 and omit size/style settings:
saving one direction is then free, and eight views charge only rotations.
A generated first frame always faces the viewer (south), whatever the
description says. For a profile or other facing with n_directions=1, make
it with create_image_pro_flash and pass its id as source_image_id.
Objects remain objects without skeletons. Poll get_object(object_id), then
download its PNG (one direction) or ZIP (eight). No preview is regenerated.

Cost: n_directions=1 is the image alone, by longest side — 5 generations up
to 96px, 6 from 100 to 208, 9 from 212 to 256 — so 32x96 and 64x48 are both
5. n_directions=8 adds a rotation charge, billed separately, and the
TOTAL by longest side is the same ladder the character tool uses:
6 for 16-88; 7 for 92-96; 8 for 100-128; 9 for 132-156; 10 for 160-180; 11 for 184-200; 12 for 204-208; 15 for 212-220; 16 for 224-236; 17 for 240-256. The steps are uneven, so read the band rather than interpolating;
get_pro_flash_capabilities(operation="object", width=, height=,
n_directions=) quotes the split for free. Reusing a first frame bills only the rotation
part, and nothing at all for one direction.

## Parameters
- `description` (str, required)
- `source_image_id` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None]
- `first_frame_base64` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None]
- `first_frame_url` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None]
- `name` (str, optional) [default: ]
- `view` (Literal["low top-down", "high top-down", "side"], optional) [default: low top-down]
- `first_frame_direction` (Literal["south"], optional) [default: south]
- `n_directions` (Literal[1, 8], optional) [default: 8]
- `seed` (int, optional) [default: 0]
- `width` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — Defaults to 64 for text creation. Native sizes: 16x16 (experimental), 24x24, 32x32, 32x48, 48x48, 64x64, 96x64, 96x96, 128x128. Custom size (Beta): integer width 16–256 and height 16–256. Both dimensions must be multiples of 4 pixels. Pixel-grid recovery uses image-to-pixel-art with fixer when needed. No native image resizing.
- `height` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None]
- `style_image` (Optional[ProFlashReferenceInput], optional) [default: None] — Style anchor. Exactly ONE of its three sources: `url` also accepts an `upload:<id>` from get_upload_url or a data: URL, and `source_image_id` is an image you own (what a Pro Flash job returns). It must fit INSIDE the output canvas both ways — a larger one is refused, so crop it; resizing pixel art is never the answer. Reuse one anchor across calls to keep a set consistent.
- `style_options` (Optional[ProFlashStyleOptions], optional) [default: None]
- `palette` (Optional[list[str]], optional) [default: None] — Target palette, 2 to 256 hex colours as a JSON array, e.g. ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"] for Game Boy or ["#000000", "#ffffff"] for 1-bit. Every pixel the tool draws is one of them; pixels you supplied (a direction you drew) stay as they are.
- `palette_name` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Optional name of the palette (e.g. 'Game Boy', 'PICO-8'); naming it helps the look. It only LABELS the colours you pass in palette rather than looking any up, so it cannot be sent on its own.
- `max_colors` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — At most this many colours (2-64). With a palette, they are picked from it. On the three tools that have a standard mode — create_character, create_topdown_tileset, animate_object — ANY palette setting needs mode='pro': standard refuses palette and max_colors, alone or together. Every other tool taking them has no standard mode and accepts them always.

## Usage
```python
create_object_pro_flash(
    description=...,
)
```

3	PIXL/2 adds explicit intake and candidate acceptance to the existing agent-operated language. Its header is `PX2 <revision>`; value framing, bounds, identifiers, canonical ordering and record hashing follow [PIXL/1](PIXL-1.md). The enclosing canonical document includes its own format header. Existing PX1 files and the [PX1 registry](../pixl/registry.json) retain their original semantics.
4	
5	The complete PX2 field/type schema is [registry-v2.json](../pixl/registry-v2.json). Fields inherited unchanged from PX1 retain their defined meanings. Unknown kinds, fields and enum values fail. The JSON host adapter may include `format: 2`; absence means 1. The lifecycle commands never guess a format from fields. Library records can be copied with their complete dependency closure without changing record hashes; validate the destination document and its actual file paths.
6	
7	PX2 shares PX1's optional [library-source retention](library-retention.md): source resolution preserves the declared revision and reports its retained identity, while choice authority, adoption, candidate and verdict semantics remain unchanged.
8	
9	## Intake and concrete contracts
10	
11	P owns a list `in` of I choices and can retain the brief in `br`. Its `ct` is optional. Initialization via `intake` creates no C, dimensions, projection, palette or alpha defaults. The user is a valid A role. Old `init` remains a PX1 initializer for compatibility.
12	
13	I has an owning project `pr`, responsible actor `wh`, key `ky`, status `st`, value `vl`, source list `so` and rationale `wy`. Keys are unique within a project. Each I must appear in its P.in and cannot appear in another project's list. Status is one of:
14	
15	| Status | Required meaning |
16	|---|---|
17	| unresolved | `vl=?`; retain the missing choice or question in `wy` |
18	| observed | Non-null value with source evidence; an observation does not establish agreement |
19	| proposed | Non-null candidate value and rationale; sources can be absent |
20	| confirmed | Non-null value and supporting source, including a retained user instruction where applicable |
21	| conflict | At least two alternatives in `vl`, with sources/rationale preserving the disagreement |
22	
23	Confirmation is a recorded claim supported by sources, not authentication of the actor. A C is a concrete raster interpretation and can link its contributing choices through `ch`. When a linked choice is usable, a key naming an existing C field must have the same value as that field; custom aesthetic choices remain explicit semantic context. A previously concrete interpretation may remain recorded when its choice becomes unresolved/conflicting, but that contract cannot support active work until the conflict is resolved. This permits preserving old candidates and evidence while recording newly discovered uncertainty. Existing sources may intentionally use another contract.
24	
25	## Planned work and materialized candidates
26	
27	PX2 T has `ph` (research/sample/production/delivery), `ip` (existing X inputs), `op` (planned F outputs), `ca` (nominated X candidates) and `vr` (retained V verdicts), alongside `nm/ow/pr/dp/dc/kn/st`. PX1 task fields `io/ev` are not PX2 fields.
28	
29	F names a planned output and its kind, owning task `tk`, applicable requirements `rq`, and optional contract `ct`. T.op and F.tk must agree. F contains no invented file identity; it can exist before work produces a file. Each F requires at least one Q. A candidate X uses `of` to identify its F and must match its kind and contract. X always names actual bytes. Report/code/reference X may omit C; raster kinds cannot.
30	
31	Research and sample phases can investigate unproven K and can lack D. An open production/delivery task can plan before adoption; activation/completion requires an evidence-backed D and passing K scope coverage. D's research/proof requirements are unchanged. All active/done tasks require their prerequisites done. Raster output plans require a concrete C before activation, and unresolved/conflicting output choices block every phase. Sample work can test proposed/observed choices; production/delivery requires all choices in its output contracts confirmed. These choices must belong to the task's project. Input reference art can have another project's style and is not forced to adopt the output contract.
32	
33	`ready` returns only open tasks with satisfied local blockers. It never establishes remote availability or acceptance. `workflow` reports unresolved intake, per-task blockers and each planned output's candidates and requirement outcomes. A report can distinguish an unperformed check, a failed check and an unavailable check without changing state.
34	
35	## Required acceptance and retained verdicts
36	
37	Q declares an observable condition `ck`, owner `wh`, sources `so`, domain `dm` and required evidence mode `md`. Domains are mechanical, visual, continuity, engine and other. Visual criteria require visual mode; engine criteria require live mode. Other domains choose their applicable mode explicitly. There is no universal requirement that every output use every domain. Requirements belong to the plan and are stated before observing the candidate's results.
38	
39	V identifies a task, candidate X, required Q, reviewer, timestamp, rationale, status and supporting E receipts. Status is pass, fail or unavailable. Absence of a current V means unperformed. An unavailable verdict records the reason with no E and cannot accept anything. Only one non-superseded V may exist for a task/candidate/criterion combination; T.vr retains every V for that task.
40	
41	Current pass/fail verdicts require non-superseded E of the matching outcome and Q's required mode. Their combined bindings cover the candidate's full semantic scope and Q's full semantic scope. Thus evidence is bound to the actual X/F/C/I/Q/source revisions, not just an artifact name or a generic fixture. Receipt mode is a caller assertion backed by a retained file; live mode does not authenticate a service or engine. A provider response or bundled method POC cannot be substituted for a visual or engine acceptance obligation by reusing its old bindings.
42	
43	Semantic traversal in PX2 excludes P/E/T/J/N/V and includes I/F/Q as well as the original semantic kinds. Changing task states or superseding V therefore does not recursively change the evidence it summarizes. Changing a contract, applicable choice, plan or criterion invalidates live E bindings. Superseded V retains its old outcome and references but no longer requires current criterion membership or current E support. This permits an explicitly revised plan to retain historical rejected or obsolete requirements.
44	
45	A done task needs all prerequisite tasks done, at least one F, exactly one nominated X per F, and a current passing V for every Q on every nominee. Mechanical success alone cannot satisfy visual or engine criteria. Older rejected candidates remain recorded and do not prevent selecting a later candidate, but no unreviewed replacement inherits their proof.
46	
47	The optional [task completion operation](task-completion.md) nominates explicit already-reviewed candidates and publishes the existing active/done transitions. It retains all acceptance checks and creates no verdict or new UDL field.
48	
49	## Publication, amendment and resumption
50	
51	All PX1 concurrency, path confinement, immutable E and history publication guarantees remain. V fields are immutable after publication except one-way `ob=+`; correcting a verdict adds a new V ID. A newly introduced V cannot already be superseded: it must first pass current validation and be published, then a later revision may supersede it. Existing IDs cannot disappear. A store rejects format changes during commit. Existing PX1 stores are not automatically upgraded because old state does not identify confirmed choices or required acceptance. Start a new explicitly authored PX2 project when these operations are needed; preserve the old project as its own source/history.
52	
53	For each newly published pass/fail V, the planned F and its complete semantic scope, including Q and C/choices, must already exist unchanged in the immediately preceding saved state. Save planning/criterion changes before collecting and publishing results. Initial PX2 publication cannot contain pass/fail V. Unavailable observations do not claim evaluation and are exempt from this ordering rule. This establishes recorded ordering between a plan and its verdict; it cannot independently attest when a person actually inspected an image.
54	
55	A done task must reopen when it or its relevant dependency closure changes. PX2 closure does not traverse through P: an unrelated intake choice or project display name does not reopen an accepted sample. Link actual semantic dependencies through its input/output contracts, choices, criteria, sources and decisions. Changing one of those dependencies requires reopening and superseding stale E/V before new evaluation. History remains available for cold resumption.
56	
57	The optional [selected-asset preparation adapter](asset-preparation.md) authors the
58	existing candidate/sample records from exact reviewed PLAR artifacts and retains
59	input bytes. Its explicit versioned report-X metadata binding also checks current
60	PLAR identity before new job preparation/dispatch; it does not add record fields or
61	relabel an expert candidate interpretation as owner-approved production.
62	
63	## Operational boundaries
64	
65	The optional [candidate/family review adapter](candidate-review.md) retains explicit
66	observations through existing X/E/V, derives exact evidence scope and connects
67	nomination/completion with recoverable publication. It adds no registry fields;
68	prepared inspection packets retain their existing coverage contract.
69	
70	The optional [connected production-plan adapter](production-plan.md) authors
71	family/stage wiring from reviewed JSON and binds exact accepted upstream inputs
72	before preparing a staged request. It uses existing T/F/Q/X and PLAR metadata;
73	contracts, adoption, provider execution and acceptance keep their existing meaning.
74	
75	Use `intake`, `decode`, `encode`, `validate`, `commit`, `workflow`, `ready`, `context` and `impact` through the selected runner; MCP adds `pixl_intake` and `pixl_workflow`. `context` retains PX2 format and complete references. Mutable state and evidence live in the art project, outside installed resources. Generic encode/commit can author the declared records; they do not perform inspection or grant approval.
76	
77	This version supplies the local intake/sample lifecycle. The original platform prepare/job tools remain stateless local operations. Real PixelLab execution, actual visual judgments, destination-engine verification and model performance require their own observed evidence.
78	
79	## Durable provider jobs (registry 2.1.0 extension)
80	
81	J opts into durable history by supplying `jr` (current journal report X), `op` (nonempty distinct F outputs) and `xs` (all imported X candidates in event order, initially empty). J.xs preserves typed dependency closure for focused retrieval; these are not task nominations. Existing J without these fields retains its earlier semantics. A published legacy J cannot acquire this extension, and a durable J cannot shed it. Older PX2 readers reject these additional fields explicitly. PX1 schema and semantics are unchanged.
82	
83	The retained journal uses the version-1 closed JSON contract in [provider-recovery.md](provider-recovery.md). J.tk/tl/ah/si/ri/op must exactly project its task/tool/intent hash/state/remote identity/outputs. J.ev retains ordered local E receipts for every snapshot, starting with prepared intent and adding one snapshot per event. Each non-superseded local passing E binds exactly its immutable journal X and shares its path/hash. The last receipt binds J.jr. Such a pass establishes retention and local consistency; it is not remote, mechanical, visual or engine acceptance.
84	
85	Generic rooted validation replays the journal and every prefix, verifies local bytes and candidate bindings, and rejects invented projections. Publication requires a saved unchanged production plan before new prepared intent, one event per subsequent commit, immutable intent, immutable retained X/E, and unchanged imported candidates. No initial-state job can invent earlier submission history. Preparation and dispatch require satisfied task activation prerequisites and an open/active task. Another nonterminal durable attempt for an overlapping output, or an unjournaled nonterminal job for the task, blocks new preparation/dispatch.
86	
87	The local dispatch claim publishes `unknown` before returning the request to its host. It does not contact a service. Unknown work must be reconciled rather than resubmitted. Caller-supplied observations retain the returned identity and evidence; accepted states require an ID, which cannot change once recorded. Failed and succeeded are terminal except that success may import new candidates. Completion never follows from provider success: imported candidates still require their declared V criteria.
88	
89	Changed request context blocks dispatch but does not erase submitted history or prevent recording observations. Recovery reports list drift and next actions. Imports bind copied local bytes and the original output plan; a changed output plan must be reconciled before import. All operations use expected-hash publication. Unreferenced immutable blobs may remain after a failed commit; state.px is the sole publication authority. Local coordination cannot guarantee exactly-once remote execution or prevent a host from bypassing the procedure.
90	
91	## Family production and delivery (registry 2.2.0 extension)
92	
93	An optional F.bs names the exact X baseline for production or delivery. It is a semantic dependency, unlike the workflow-only T.ip. The baseline must belong to another sample task in the same project; its X is also listed in the consuming task's ip, and its task is a direct dp prerequisite. Open plans may preserve an unaccepted or replaced baseline. Activation/completion requires that exact sample still nominated and its task done. A sample's passing evidence does not automatically accept a family member.
94	
95	F.mb and F.ds together opt a report-kind output of a delivery task into the family operation and require bs. mb is a nonempty distinct ordered list of planned F members; ds is a nonempty distinct list of same-project I destination choices. Members cannot be the family output itself or another family output. They are the baseline's sample output or same-project production outputs sharing that exact bs. All member tasks are direct delivery prerequisites. A family declares at least one continuity Q, with project-specific mode/conditions; engine Q is declared when applicable. All destination choices must be confirmed for delivery activation/completion. Missing/unavailable engine acceptance remains separately represented through Q/V.
96	
97	A family manifest X has xs: baseline X first, then one selected X per member in the saved order (the baseline may also be a delivered member). xs belongs only to family report candidates and is required on every candidate of a family output. These references bind collective acceptance to the actual baseline, selected member identities, their plans/contracts and the destination/criteria scope. Merely listing siblings in T.ip does not supply this semantic proof.
98	
99	The [family delivery manifest contract](family-delivery.md) governs immutable copied files, saved-plan publication, historical membership and current acceptance. Existing family F cannot shed bs/mb/ds, and existing X cannot acquire fabricated snapshot history. Once published, a manifest X and its baseline/member X records are immutable; revisions add new candidate IDs. Changes to underlying contracts/requirements still require the existing supersession/reopening procedure.
100	
101	`family` / `pixl_family` reports baseline eligibility, member and collective acceptance, destination choices, pending provider attempts, saved snapshots and drift. `family-snapshot` / `pixl_family_snapshot` retains selected member bytes and publishes an unaccepted report candidate. It requires an open/active family task, the accepted baseline and all selected members on done tasks, no pending attempts for involved tasks, and the unchanged previously saved family plan. Snapshotting local files is allowed while destination/adoption/collective acceptance remains unresolved; it does not activate, nominate, evaluate or complete the delivery task. Actual artistic continuity and target-engine readiness require their own inspection and evidence.
102	
103	PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.
